questions.question: React vs Angular vs Vue — what are the differences?
questions.title: React vs Angular vs Vue — Differences, Trade-offs (2026)
questions.direct_answer:
React vs Angular vs Vue — what are the differences?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** React: library, unopinionated; Angular: full framework, TypeScript-first, RxJS, DI; Vue: progressive, SFCs, template-first; ecosystems, job markets, perf profiles.

**Classic weak answer:** Declaring one 'the best' — each wins in different team/product contexts; avoid absolute statements.

**Senior finish:** Give 2026-accurate market shares (React largest, Angular second in enterprise, Vue strong in Asia), and note Svelte/SolidJS as rising alternatives.

interviewer_intent.testing: React: library, unopinionated; Angular: full framework, TypeScript-first, RxJS, DI; Vue: progressive, SFCs, template-first; ecosystems, job markets, perf profiles
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Declaring one 'the best' — each wins in different team/product contexts; avoid absolute statements
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Give 2026-accurate market shares (React largest, Angular second in enterprise, Vue strong in Asia), and note Svelte/SolidJS as rising alternatives

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **React vs Angular vs Vue — Differences, Trade-offs (2026)** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** React vs Angular vs Vue — what are the differences?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **React: library, unopinionated; Angular: full framework, TypeScript-first, RxJS, DI; Vue: progressive, SFCs, template-first; ecosystems, job markets, perf profiles**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Declaring one 'the best' — each wins in different team/product contexts; avoid absolute statements**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Give 2026-accurate market shares (React largest, Angular second in enterprise, Vue strong in Asia), and note Svelte/SolidJS as rising alternatives**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** React: library, unopinionated; Angular: full framework, TypeScript-first, RxJS, DI; Vue: progressive, SFCs, template-first; ecosystems, job markets, perf profiles
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **declaring one 'the best' — each wins in different team/product contexts; avoid absolute statements** and what you do instead.

questions.question: After hooks, should you still use class components in React?
questions.title: Class vs Functional Components After Hooks — 2026 Recommendation
questions.direct_answer:
After hooks, should you still use class components in React?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Function components with hooks are the default; class components remain supported but not recommended for new code.

**Classic weak answer:** Mixing classes and functions without a plan — pick one convention per module; new code should be functional.

**Senior finish:** Note that Error Boundaries still need a class component (until a hook equivalent lands); everything else is functional.

interviewer_intent.testing: Function components with hooks are the default; class components remain supported but not recommended for new code
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Mixing classes and functions without a plan — pick one convention per module; new code should be functional
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Note that Error Boundaries still need a class component (until a hook equivalent lands); everything else is functional

questions.question: Redux vs Context API vs Zustand — when should you use each?
questions.title: Redux vs Context API vs Zustand — When to Use Each (2026)
questions.direct_answer:
Redux vs Context API vs Zustand — when should you use each?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Context: simple sharing, re-render all consumers; Redux: time-travel, middleware, large apps; Zustand: lightweight, selector-based, minimal boilerplate.

**Classic weak answer:** Always reaching for Redux first — for most small/medium apps, Zustand or React Query + Context is enough.

**Senior finish:** Also mention Jotai (atomic) and Redux Toolkit (Redux + Immer + minimal boilerplate) as practical modern picks.
